Journal of Educational Research · Vol. 14 · Issue 2 DOI: 10.0000/jer.2026.0142

Generative AI Feedback and Academic Reading Comprehension in Higher Education: A Six-Week Observational Study

M. Rivera1, L. Chen2, & A. Morales1

1 Center for Learning Sciences  ·  2 Department of Educational Technology

Abstract · Resumen Original · Inglés

Keywords: generative AI, academic reading, guided feedback, higher education, structured prompts

1. Introduction

University students increasingly interact with large language models while reading dense scientific literature. Prior descriptive studies have documented rapid adoption, yet the relationship between guided prompting practices and comprehension outcomes remains actively investigated across disciplines.

2. Study Context

To examine authentic academic reading workflows, we followed undergraduate cohorts during a six-week seminar module. Participants logged weekly summaries and received structured scaffolding aligned with disciplinary reading rubrics.

Original · EN

This observational study examined the association between guided AI feedback and academic reading comprehension in 120 undergraduate students over six weeks. A moderate positive correlation was observed, although causal effects could not be established. These findings suggest that structured prompts may support comprehension, but larger randomized trials are still needed.
